citation: Halperin I, Malleron T, Har-Nir I, Androulakis-Korakakis P, Wolf M, Fisher J, Steele J. Accuracy in predicting repetitions to task failure in resistance exercise: a scoping review and exploratory meta-analysis. Sports Med 2022;52(2):377-390
status: published; no retraction found (A6 CORRECTED ROW)
results_effects_uncertainty: Mean signed UNDERprediction 0.95 reps (95% CI 0.17-1.73); I2 97.9%; between-participant SD ~1.45 reps; more accurate closer to failure, with heavier loads/fewer reps, later sets; training status no clear effect
limitations_coi: 0.95 is a BIAS not an MAE; failure definitions vary
tentsr_applicability: Benchmark for TENSR RIR must be measured self-report MAE (raw and bias-corrected), not 0.95; humans best near failure = the zone that matters

citation: Mills KR. Power spectral analysis of electromyogram and compound muscle action potential during muscle fatigue and recovery. J Physiol 1982;326:401-409 (bibliographic details from memory; content via search snippet)
results_effects_uncertainty: Force and action-potential amplitude recovery half-complete at ~30 s; MPF and relaxation rate half-complete at ~3 min; spectral recovery tied to metabolic state
tentsr_applicability: Contradicts A2's 'MDF recovers faster than force': dissociation direction is paradigm-dependent; spectral rest timer unvalidated either way

citation: Zhao H, et al. (Okada J group, Waseda). Power bench press: RPE, velocity loss and spectral fatigue index. Int J Sports Med 2025;46(6):437-445
results_effects_uncertainty: Spectral fatigue index vs velocity loss r=0.603; vs RPE r=0.547; RPE vs VL r=0.667
limitations_coi: correlations at group level; n not retrieved
tentsr_applicability: Counterweight to A4's Zhao2025 (PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.20426) null MDF-VL finding from the same group

citation: Zhao H, Kurokawa T, Tajima M, Liu Z, Okada J. Perceived exertion in power-aimed resistance training (central vs peripheral). PeerJ 2025 (A6 CORRECTED: journal/DOI confirmed)
results_effects_uncertainty: No significant MDF-velocity-loss relation reported
tentsr_applicability: Do not cite alone as evidence MDF is unrelated to velocity loss

citation: Oliveira AS, Goncalves M. Neuromuscular recovery of the biceps brachii muscle after resistance exercise. Res Sports Med 2008;16(4):244-256 (A6 CORRECTED: authors identified; = A2 BicepsRecovery2008)
exercise_muscle_contraction: biceps curl, four 1-min bouts at 25/30/35/40% 1RM, 10 min rest; reference contraction 50% MVC
results_effects_uncertainty: RMS up, MDF down immediately; most variables near reference after ~1 min; load did not alter recovery
limitations_coi: NOT sets to failure; no force-recovery measure, so cannot show EMG-force dissociation
tentsr_applicability: Weak support only for 'EMG spectral variables recover in ~1 min after light work'

citation: Elfving B, Liljequist D, Dedering A, Nemeth G. Recovery of electromyograph median frequency after lumbar muscle fatigue analysed using an exponential time dependence model. Eur J Appl Physiol 2002 (A6: identifies A2 MDFRecovery_Lumbar)
exercise_muscle_contraction: isometric back extension 80% MVC 45 s, recovery probes
results_effects_uncertainty: Exponential recovery model fitted in most healthy subjects
limitations_coi: pH/force dissociation claim NOT found in retrieved record
tentsr_applicability: Does not support A2's dissociation claim as cited

citation: Kassiano W, et al. Greater gastrocnemius muscle hypertrophy after partial range of motion training performed at long muscle lengths. J Strength Cond Res 2023;37(9):1746-1753 (A6 CORRECTED numbers)
exercise_muscle_contraction: calf raise full vs lengthened partial vs shortened partial
results_effects_uncertainty: Lengthened partial largest medial gastrocnemius gain; shortened partial +6.2%, full +7.3% (lengthened value not retrieved). A1's +15.2/+6.7/+3.4% NOT supported (6.7% is from a different 2025 study)
tentsr_applicability: as A1

citation: Colyer SL, McGuigan PM. Textile electrodes embedded in clothing: a practical alternative to traditional surface electromyography when assessing muscle excitation during functional movements. J Sports Sci Med 2018;17(1):101-109 (A6 CORRECTED)
hardware_processing: textile EMG shorts vs Delsys Trigno DRY silver-bar surface sensors (NOT gel)
results_effects_uncertainty: Within-session ARV CV 13.8% (textile) vs 14.1% (surface); BETWEEN-session ARV CV 42.6% vs 41.2%; poorer agreement at higher excitation; textile bursts consistently longer
limitations_coi: reference not gel; no LoA in abstract
tentsr_applicability: Day-to-day un-normalised amplitude ~40% CV even for a research dry system: no between-day amplitude feature without normalisation; burst timing device-specific

citation: Lynn SK, Watkins CM, Wong MA, Balfany K, Feeney DF. Validity and reliability of surface electromyography measurements from a wearable athlete performance system. J Sports Sci Med 2018;17:205-215 (A6 CORRECTED: n and task)
design: validity + reliability, 7 sessions on separate days
exercise_muscle_contraction: isokinetic knee ext/flex; VL, VM, BF
hardware_processing: Athos garment vs research sEMG concurrently
results_effects_uncertainty: No significant system effect on rep amplitude; torque-EMG relation not different; between-trial variation higher for Athos by 0.8% (BF), 7.3% (VL), 0.2% (VM)
limitations_coi: n=12; non-significance not equivalence; Athos-affiliated authors (COI)
tentsr_applicability: Amplitude only, isokinetic; nothing spectral; does not transfer to 7 mm dry studs on a band

citation: Nishihara K, et al. Investigation of innervation zone shift with continuous dynamic muscle contraction. Comput Math Methods Med 2013 (A6: DOI confirmed)
results_effects_uncertainty: IZ shift 3.9 mm (acute elbow angles) vs 16 mm (obtuse)
tentsr_applicability: IZ can cross a 25.4 mm detection volume within a rep; phase-locked windows required

citation: Thomas J, Wahlstrom J. Estimation of resistance training RPE using inertial sensors and electromyography. arXiv 2510.03197 (2025) PREPRINT (A6: authors confirmed)
results_effects_uncertainty: EMG slightly improved accuracy over IMU alone; eccentric rep time strongest predictor
limitations_coi: preprint; subjective label; validation scheme not retrieved
tentsr_applicability: EMG may add little over the puck IMU: IMU-only baseline mandatory

citation: Jukic I, et al. Modeling the repetitions-in-reserve-velocity relationship: a valid method for resistance training monitoring and prescription, and fatigue management. Physiol Rep 2024 (A6: n confirmed)
exercise_muscle_contraction: free-weight back squat; 1RM + two RTF tests 72 h apart
results_effects_uncertainty: Individual (not general) RIR-velocity relationships from session 1 predicted RIR in session 2 with mean error <2 reps regardless of load
limitations_coi: single exercise; error metric definition not retrieved
tentsr_applicability: Best objective precedent reaches <2 reps; no sensor precedent beats bias-corrected self-report

citation: Tsoukos A, et al. Changes in EMG and movement velocity during a set to failure against different loads in the bench press exercise. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2021 (A6: = A4 SJMSS2021bench)
exercise_muscle_contraction: bench press to failure, max intended velocity, 40/60/80% 1RM
results_effects_uncertainty: MDF drop and mean velocity loss at exhaustion greater at 40% and 60% than 80% (p<0.05)
tentsr_applicability: No fixed MDF value at failure across loads

citation: Gerdle B, Fugl-Meyer AR. Is the mean power frequency shift of the EMG a selective indicator of fatigue of the fast twitch motor units? Acta Physiol Scand 1992;145(2):129-138 (A6 CORRECTED)
exercise_muscle_contraction: repeated isokinetic plantar flexion; 3 plantar flexors
results_effects_uncertainty: Output and RMS fell without significant MPF fall under hypoxia; MPF shift mainly reflects type II fibre biochemistry; type I/hypoxic fatigue not detected
limitations_coi: small; later work (Gerdle & Elert 1994) questions timing
tentsr_applicability: MPF/MDF can miss part of fatigue: spectral trend is not a complete fatigue measure

citation: Weakley J, Till K, Sampson J, Banyard H, Leduc C, Wilson K, Roe G, Jones B. The effects of augmented feedback on sprint, jump, and strength adaptations in rugby union players after a 4-week training program. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2019;14(9):1205-1211
exercise_muscle_contraction: resistance training with velocity feedback + jump/sprint feedback
results_effects_uncertainty: CMJ RPP ES 0.34+/-0.42, 10 m 0.20+/-0.35, 20 m 0.40+/-0.21, 3RM squat 0.23+/-0.17 possibly-likely greater (MBI)
tentsr_applicability: Feedback can change chronic outcomes a little; sign of TENSR cue error matters

citation: Weakley J, et al. The effect of feedback on resistance training performance and adaptations: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Med 2023;53(9):1789-1803 (A6 CORRECTED: chronic conclusion added)
results_effects_uncertainty: Velocity +8.4% (g 0.63, 0.36-0.90); visual g 1.11 vs verbal 0.47; authors conclude chronic feedback gave greater speed/strength/jump/technique adaptations
tentsr_applicability: Feedback raises acute effort reliably: a biased RIR cue will push users harder

citation: Augustin F, Pinero A, Enes A, Mohan AE, Sapuppo M, Coleman M, Wolf M, Androulakis Korakakis P, Swinton PA, Nippard J, Schoenfeld BJ. Do cheaters prosper? Int J Exerc Sci 2025;18(3):329-342 (A6 CORRECTED author order)
exercise_muscle_contraction: unilateral DB curl + cable pushdown, strict vs momentum
results_effects_uncertainty: Momentum neither helped nor hindered hypertrophy; more volume load
tentsr_applicability: as A1

citation: Maeo S, et al. Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci 2023;23(7):1240-1250 (A6 CORRECTED)
exercise_muscle_contraction: cable elbow extension overhead vs neutral, 70% 1RM, 5x10, 2/wk
results_effects_uncertainty: Long head +28.5% vs +19.6% (1.5x, d=0.61); lateral+medial +14.6% vs +10.5% (1.4x, d=0.39); whole-muscle +19.9/+13.9% (A1) NOT confirmed
tentsr_applicability: as A1

citation: Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Robinson ZP, Hinson SR, Zourdos MC. The resistance training dose response: meta-regressions exploring the effects of weekly volume and frequency on muscle hypertrophy and strength gains. Sports Med 2026;56(2):481-505
doi_or_link: DOI 10.1007/s40279-025-02344-w UNVERIFIABLE (exact-string search returned nothing); SportRxiv preprint exists
results_effects_uncertainty: Unique dose-response for volume vs hypertrophy and strength; strength more diminishing returns; frequency effects identifiable for strength only; fractional set counting best-supported
tentsr_applicability: Weekly sets per instrumented muscle is the defensible dose metric; compound lifts feed other muscles fractionally

citation: Garofalo L, Defauw S, Calcagno G, (Fiorilli G per repository). Estimating proximity to muscular failure using surface EMG and deep learning. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 2026
comparator_reference: linear regression and SVR baselines; time-to-failure
results_effects_uncertainty: Authors conclude proximity to failure estimable in isometric holds; '87%' from aggregator UNVERIFIED; validation scheme and MSE units UNVERIFIED
tentsr_applicability: Not evidence for dynamic RIR

citation: A6 derived analysis: sensitivity of A3 sinc3/MDF model to spectral shape; truncation vs droop vs inverse-sinc compensation; bipolar dip on relative change; slope precision; A5 sample-size recomputation (A6-check-mdf.py, A6-check-stats.py)
status: internal derived analysis, not peer reviewed
hardware_processing: sinc3 model of ADS1292R; 5 model EMG spectra
results_effects_uncertainty: 500 SPS raw drop -15.6 to -17.7% (true -25%); with inverse-sinc3 -21.4 to -24.2%; 2 kSPS -23.8 to -24.2%. Bipolar dip: relative drop -25.4% (25.4 mm) vs -25.0% (20 mm). Slope t=2.1 only at 8 reps (SD 9.3 Hz, 3 Hz/rep). Bonett, Wilson, LoA, SEM, RCT n all reproduce A5
limitations_coi: model spectra, stationary Gaussian, single-CV idealisation
tentsr_applicability: 500 SPS biased but partly correctable; choose 2 kSPS; MDF trend only post-set
